name: Absalom
overview: Absalom was a male member of the tribe of Judah and the third-born son of King David. His life is marked by significant familial and political turmoil within the royal household. No additional personal notes are provided beyond his lineage and tribal affiliation.
namesAndTitles: The name Absalom means 'father is peace,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name given not by God but recorded in Scripture. This name is noted in 2 Samuel 3:3 and carries a poignant contrast to his tumultuous life.
familyAndRelationships: Absalom was the son of King David and Maacah, making him part of the royal family of Judah. He was also the brother and father of Tamar, indicating complex family dynamics. His death was caused by Joab, as recorded in 2 Samuel 18:14.
scriptureSignificance: Absalom's story highlights the tragic consequences of rebellion and familial strife within the house of David. His actions against his half-brother and his subsequent revolt against his father illustrate the dangers of unchecked ambition and broken family relationships. Despite his betrayal, the narrative underscores the enduring love and sorrow of a father toward his son, enriching the biblical portrayal of human weakness and divine sovereignty.

keyEvents.event: Fled to Geshur for three years
